max_area.py.description: After moving left, compares nums[left] to nums[right - 1] instead of nums[left - 1], so a taller left line is skipped. max_area([1, 5, 10, 6]) returns 3 instead of 10.

three_sum.py.description: After finding a triplet, left is not advanced past equal values, so the same triplet is added twice. three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0) returns [[0, 2, -2], [0, 2, -2]].

palindrome.py.description: When the left pointer meets the right one while skipping non-alphanumeric characters, the function returns False instead of True. is_palindrome('a,,a') and is_palindrome(',,,') return False.
Dead code: the right skip loop always stops on the character the left pointer already found, so this return False can never run. Unreachable for every string up to length 8 over 'a', 'b', ','.

product_except_self.py.description: [] * len(nums) creates empty lists, so the first index assignment raises IndexError. Should be [1] * len(nums).
The skip condition checks i == len(nums), which is never true, so the first iteration reads right_reuslts[len(nums)] and raises IndexError. Should be i == len(nums) - 1.

user_utils.py.description: not (flags ^ flags) is always True, so the second condition does nothing. The function is still correct: it returns bool(flags & 8).

store.py.description: process_payment records raw_subtotal (before discount and tax) as charged_amount instead of total_amount. With 1 Laptop and SUMMER10 the record says 1200.0 instead of 1263.6.
validate_cart checks stock per entry, not per item total. Two entries of item_01 with quantity 6 pass with stock 10; the second deduct_stock then does nothing, so 12 are sold and stock ends at 4.
calculate_total ignores the ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting. With it set to False, SUMMER10 still gives 1263.6 for 1 Laptop instead of 1404.0.

cart.py.description: Tax is computed on subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal. With one item at 100.0 and a 50% discount, checkout returns 60.0 instead of 55.0.

cache.py.description: set stores the caller's object without a copy. Changing the dict after set("k", d) changes what get("k") returns, so it is not the value as it was when set was called.
get returns the stored object itself. Changing the returned dict changes the cache, so the next get returns the changed value. Fixing set alone does not fix this.

rbac.py.description: has_permission checks only direct parents, not their parents. With admin -> editor -> viewer, viewer does not get admin's permissions. No explicit contract: 'hierarchical role inheritance' in the class docstring is the only hint.

locks.py.description: release does not check the lease. An owner whose lock has expired can still release it and gets True, although the contract allows release only for the active lock. ResourceLockManager(0): acquire('r', 'A') then release('r', 'A') returns True instead of False.

user_session.py.description: get_session_metadata returns the whole session record (token, metadata, created_at) instead of the metadata, and so also hands out the session token. No docstring: the method name is the only contract.
The token is built from the user id and a timestamp in seconds, so it can be guessed. A real issue, labeled so a bug report here counts as miscategorized, not as a false positive.

tax.py.description: The rates are swapped: VIP users should pay 10% tax and regular users 17%. No docstring, so only asking (or guessing from the domain) can find it. compute_total_with_tax(100, True) returns 117.0 instead of 110.0.

issues.title: Wrong comparison when moving the left pointer skips valid containers
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code compares `nums[left]` with `nums[right - 1]`. The right-pointer branch on line 25 compares the new line with the one it just left, `nums[right + 1]`. The left branch should do the same and compare with `nums[left - 1]`. As written, it can set `calc_area_flag` to False for a line that is taller than the previous one, so a better container is never evaluated. The function then returns too small a value.
issues.example: max_area([0, 2, 5]) returns 0, but the correct answer is 2, from the lines at positions 1 and 2.
issues.fix: Use `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:` on line 31. Alternatively, drop the flag and always compute the area.
issues.test_code: assert max_area([0, 2, 5]) == 2, max_area([0, 2, 5])

issues.title: Wrong comparison when moving the left pointer skips valid areas
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code compares `nums[left]` with `nums[right - 1]`. The right-pointer branch compares the new line with the one just removed, so this should compare with `nums[left - 1]`. The wrong comparison sets `calc_area_flag` to False when the new left line is tall enough to give a larger area. That area is never evaluated, so the function returns a result that is too small.
issues.example: max_area([1, 6, 6]) returns 2, but the correct answer is 6, from the two lines of height 6 at distance 1.
issues.fix: Change the condition to `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:`. Alternatively, remove the flag and compute the area on every iteration.
issues.test_code: assert max_area([1, 6, 6]) == 6, max_area([1, 6, 6])

issues.title: Wrong neighbour compared when skipping after moving the left pointer
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code compares `nums[left]` with `nums[right - 1]`. It should compare it with the line it just left, `nums[left - 1]`. This mirrors the right-pointer branch, which correctly compares `nums[right]` with `nums[right + 1]`. Because of this, `calc_area_flag` is wrongly set to False and valid candidate areas are skipped. The function then returns a result that is too small.
issues.example: max_area([0, 1, 2, 5, 2]) returns 2, but the correct answer is 4, from the lines at indices 1 and 4 (height 1, width 3) or at indices 2 and 4 (height 2, width 2).
issues.fix: Use `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:` so a candidate is skipped only when the new left line is no taller than the previous one.
issues.test_code:
r = max_area([0, 1, 2, 5, 2])
assert r == 4, r

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned: no duplicate skipping for left/right after a match
issues.explanation: The docstring says the result must not contain the same triplet twice. Only the outer index `i` skips duplicate values. After a match, `left` and `right` move by one and do not skip equal values. Repeated values in the middle of the array therefore produce the same triplet more than once.
issues.fix: After recording a match, advance `left` while nums[left] == nums[left-1] (with left < right). Also move `right` down while nums[right] == nums[right+1].
issues.test_code:
res = three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0)
norm = [tuple(sorted(t)) for t in res]
assert len(norm) == len(set(norm)), res

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: `nums.sort()` mutates the caller's list. The docstring does not say whether the input may be modified, so this is a side effect that callers may not expect, not a bug.
issues.fix: Use `nums = sorted(nums)` to leave the caller's list unchanged.

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned after a match
issues.explanation: After a match, left and right each move one step. They don't skip over repeated values. Duplicate values on either side therefore produce the same triplet again. The docstring says the result must not contain the same triplet twice. Only the outer index `i` is de-duplicated.
issues.fix: After recording a match, advance left while nums[left] == nums[left-1], and decrease right while nums[right] == nums[right+1]. Alternatively, collect the triplets in a set of tuples.
issues.test_code:
res = three_sum([-2,0,0,2,2], 0)
assert len(res) == 1, res
assert len({tuple(sorted(t)) for t in res}) == len(res), res

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: The function assumes the caller doesn't mind nums being mutated. The docstring doesn't mention this. Using sorted(nums) would avoid the side effect.
issues.fix: Use nums = sorted(nums) at the start of the function.

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned: left/right duplicates not skipped after a match
issues.explanation: After a match, left and right each move by one position without skipping equal values. Only the outer index i skips duplicates. With repeated values, the same triplet is appended more than once. This breaks the docstring rule that the result must not contain the same triplet twice.
issues.fix: After appending, advance left while nums[left] == nums[left-1] and left < right. Also move right down while nums[right] == nums[right+1] and left < right. Alternatively, store sorted tuples in a set.
issues.test_code:
r = three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0)
assert len(r) == 1, r
r2 = three_sum([0, 0, 0, 0], 0)
assert len(r2) == 1, r2

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: nums.sort() mutates the caller's list. This assumes callers don't mind their list being reordered, and the docstring doesn't mention it.
issues.fix: Use nums = sorted(nums), or document the mutation.

issues.title: Returns False when the remaining characters are all non-alphanumeric
issues.explanation: When the left pointer reaches the right pointer while still on a skipped character, the code returns False. It should return True, because nothing is left to compare. So "a!!a" fails: after the outer a's match, the remaining "!!" makes the function return False. A string with no letters or digits, such as "!!", also returns False, which contradicts the docstring. The same check on line 21 has the same problem.
issues.example: is_palindrome("a!!a") and is_palindrome("!!")
issues.fix: Return True instead of False when left_index >= right_index in both inner loops. A cleaner option is to guard the inner loops with `left_index < right_index and not word[left_index].isalnum()` and then re-check the outer loop condition.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("a!!a") is True, is_palindrome("a!!a")
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome("") is True

issues.title: Returns False when the remaining middle section has no alphanumerics
issues.explanation: When the pointers meet inside a run of skipped characters, the code returns False. The docstring says skipped characters are ignored, so the remaining middle section is empty and the result should be True. The right-hand loop at line 21 has the same early return. Both come from the same mistake, and the fix is to return True there.
issues.example: is_palindrome("a!!a") returns False. So do is_palindrome("!!") and is_palindrome("ab, ,ba").
issues.fix: Return True instead of False in both inner loops when left_index >= right_index. Alternatively, add `left_index < right_index` to the inner while conditions and let the outer loop end.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("a!!a") is True, is_palindrome("a!!a")
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome("ab, ,ba") is True, is_palindrome("ab, ,ba")

issues.title: Strings with two or more non-alphanumeric characters and no letters or digits return False
issues.explanation: The docstring says a string with no letters or digits is a palindrome. When the skip loops meet without finding an alphanumeric character, the code returns False instead of True. The same early return at line 22 has the same problem.
issues.example: is_palindrome("!!") returns False. is_palindrome(", ") and is_palindrome("...") also return False.
issues.fix: Replace the inner skip loops with `while left_index < right_index and not word[left_index].isalnum(): left_index += 1`, and do the same for the right index. After both loops, `break` or return True if `left_index >= right_index`.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome(", ") is True, is_palindrome(", ")
assert is_palindrome("...") is True, is_palindrome("...")

issues.title: Result lists are created empty, so every call raises IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * n` is `[]`, not a list of length n. The first assignment `left_results[i] = ...` raises IndexError. The prefix and suffix arrays also need a base value of 1, and an empty list can't supply it. The same mistake is repeated on lines 7 and 8, but these lines must be fixed together.
issues.example: product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4])
issues.fix: Use `left_results = [1] * len(nums)`, `right_results = [1] * len(nums)` and `results = [1] * len(nums)`.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4]) == [24, 12, 8, 6]

issues.title: Wrong boundary check in the right-to-left loop reads out of range
issues.explanation: The loop starts at i = len(nums)-1, but the guard tests `i == len(nums)`, which is never true. For i = n-1 the code reads `right_reuslts[n]` and `nums[n]`, which raises IndexError even if the lists were initialized correctly. The guard should skip i == n-1, or the loop should start at n-2.
issues.example: product_except_self([2, 3]) after the initialization is fixed to use [1]*n
issues.fix: Loop `for i in range(len(nums) - 2, -1, -1)` and drop the dead check.
issues.test_code:
import re
src = open(__file__).read() if '__file__' in globals() else ''
# Behavioral check: correct code returns the right answer for a 2-element input
assert product_except_self([2, 3]) == [3, 2]

issues.title: Typo in variable name `right_reuslts`
issues.explanation: The name is misspelled, which makes the code harder to read and search.
issues.fix: Rename it to `right_results`.

issues.title: Result lists are built empty, so every call raises IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * len(nums)` is still `[]`. The first indexed assignment, `left_results[i] = ...`, raises IndexError. The lists also need a starting value of 1, because `left_results[0]` and the last right product are empty products. `right_reuslts` and `results` on lines 7–8 have the same problem. They are fixed by the same change, so I'm reporting them as one bug.
issues.example: product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4]) raises IndexError: list index out of range
issues.fix: Use `left_results = [1] * len(nums)`, `right_results = [1] * len(nums)` and `results = [1] * len(nums)`.
issues.test_code:
r = product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4])
assert r == [24, 12, 8, 6], r

issues.title: Right-product loop starts at the last index and reads past the end
issues.explanation: The loop starts at `i = len(nums) - 1` and reads `right_reuslts[i + 1]` and `nums[i + 1]`, which are out of range. The guard `i == len(nums)` can never be true, because `i` never reaches `len(nums)`. The loop should start at `len(nums) - 2`. Fixing the list initialization alone would still raise IndexError here.
issues.example: With the lists initialized to [1]*n, product_except_self([2, 3]) still raises IndexError at i=1.
issues.fix: Iterate `for i in range(len(nums) - 2, -1, -1)` and remove the dead guard.
issues.test_code:
r = product_except_self([2, 3])
assert r == [3, 2], r

issues.title: Misspelled variable name and unused loop variable
issues.explanation: `right_reuslts` is a typo for `right_results`. The `num` loop variable on line 10 is unused, and the `if i == 0: continue` pattern is clumsy.
issues.fix: Rename it to `right_results` and iterate with `range(1, len(nums))`.

issues.title: Result lists are created empty, so every call crashes with IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * n` is `[]`, not a list of n elements. The later indexed assignments, such as `left_results[i] = ...` on line 13, raise IndexError. The function fails for every valid input. The same mistake is on lines 7 and 8. The lists also need initial values of 1 for the prefix and suffix products.
issues.example: product_except_self([1,2,3,4])
issues.fix: Use `left_results = [1] * len(nums)`, `right_results = [1] * len(nums)` and `results = [1] * len(nums)`.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([1,2,3,4]) == [24,12,8,6], product_except_self([1,2,3,4])

issues.title: Right-product loop starts at the last index and reads out of bounds
issues.explanation: The loop starts at i = len(nums)-1 and reads `nums[i+1]` and `right_reuslts[i+1]`, which are out of range. The guard `i == len(nums)` can never be true because i never reaches len(nums). The loop should start at len(nums)-2. This would raise IndexError even if the lists were initialized correctly.
issues.example: product_except_self([2,3])
issues.fix: Iterate `for i in range(len(nums) - 2, -1, -1)` and remove the dead guard.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([2,3]) == [3,2], product_except_self([2,3])

issues.title: Typo in variable name and unnecessary arrays
issues.explanation: `right_reuslts` is misspelled. Three separate arrays are also used where one result array and a running suffix product would do.
issues.fix: Rename it to `right_results`, or use a single result list plus a running right product.

issues.title: Trivial helpers and parameters named `dict` shadow the builtin
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` only wrap a single dict operation. Their parameters, and the local variable at line 16, are named `dict`, which shadows the builtin type. The function names also use camelCase instead of snake_case. The algorithm itself is correct: it returns i<j, handles duplicates, and returns [] when no pair exists.
issues.fix: Inline the dict operations and rename the variable to something like `seen`. For example, use `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`.

issues.title: Parameter named `dict` shadows the builtin, and the helper functions add nothing
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` only wrap a single dict assignment and a single lookup. Both use `dict` as a parameter name, and `two_sum` uses it as a local variable, so the builtin is shadowed in all three. The helper names are camelCase, which does not match the snake_case of `two_sum`. The algorithm itself is correct: it is a one-pass hash map, it handles duplicates, and it returns i < j.
issues.fix: Inline the helpers as `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`. Rename the variable to something like `seen`.

issues.title: Parameters named `dict` shadow the builtin, and the helper functions add nothing
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` are one-line wrappers around dict operations. They use camelCase, which is not PEP 8 style. Their parameter `dict`, and the local variable `dict` in `two_sum`, hide the builtin type. The algorithm itself is correct. For example, `[3,3]` with target 6 returns `[0,1]`, and an input with no pair returns `[]`.
issues.fix: Inline the wrappers as `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`. Rename the variable `dict` to something like `seen`.

issues.title: Redundant always-true condition in bit check
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. It does nothing and suggests a validity check that doesn't exist. The result is the same as `bool(flags & (1 << 3))`, so the docstring is met. The `is_valid` name is also misleading. This assumes bit 3 is zero-indexed, which is the value 8.
issues.example: check_bitwise_flags(8) returns True and check_bitwise_flags(7) returns False, with or without the extra term.
issues.fix: Use `return bool(flags & (1 << 3))` and drop the `is_valid` variable.

issues.title: Redundant always-true condition `not (flags ^ flags)`
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. The result is still correct, because it equals whether bit 3 is set. The extra clause is dead code and suggests a check that is not actually done. The temporary variable `is_valid` is also unnecessary. This assumes that 'bit 3' means zero-indexed bit 3, which is mask 8.
issues.fix: return bool(flags & (1 << 3))

issues.title: Redundant `not (flags ^ flags)` clause
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. The function still returns the right answer, which is whether bit 3 is set, but the extra clause is dead code and suggests a check that doesn't exist. The function also assumes bit 3 is zero-indexed, meaning the mask 8. The docstring doesn't say this.
issues.fix: Use `return bool(flags & (1 << 3))`.

issues.title: validate_cart checks each entry separately, so duplicate item_ids can oversell
issues.explanation: The docstring says stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item, and the same item_id may appear in several entries. Each entry is checked against stock on its own. Two entries of 6 for an item with 10 in stock both pass. In process_payment, the second deduct_stock then silently does nothing because stock is short. The customer is charged for goods that were never deducted from stock.
issues.example: validate_cart([{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}]) returns True, but item_01 has only 10 in stock.
issues.fix: Sum quantities per item_id first, then check stock against each total. Return False if any total exceeds stock.
issues.test_code:
inv=InventoryService();p=PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(),inv)
r=p.validate_cart([{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}])
assert r is False, r

issues.title: ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting is ignored in calculate_total
issues.explanation: The docstring says a discount code applies only when ENABLE_DISCOUNTS is on. The code never reads that setting, so discounts are applied even when it is off.
issues.example: With ENABLE_DISCOUNTS=False, calculate_total([{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":2}], "SUMMER10") returns 52.65. The correct value is 58.5.
issues.fix: Read ConfigurationRegistry.get("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True) and apply the discount only when it is truthy.
issues.test_code:
ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", False)
try:
    p=PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(),InventoryService())
    r=p.calculate_total([{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":2}],"SUMMER10")
    assert r == 58.5, r
finally:
    ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True)

issues.title: charged_amount records the raw subtotal instead of the amount charged
issues.explanation: The docstring says charged_amount is the amount actually charged, as returned by calculate_total. The code stores raw_subtotal, which has no discount and no tax. total_amount is computed and then never used. AuditService.verify_user_totals therefore returns wrong sums.
issues.example: Paying for 2 Mouse (item_02) with SUMMER10 records charged_amount 50.0. calculate_total returns 52.65.
issues.fix: Use "charged_amount": total_amount and remove the raw_subtotal computation.
issues.test_code:
sm=SessionManager();p=PaymentProcessor(sm,InventoryService())
s=sm.create_session("u")
items=[{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":2}]
expected=p.calculate_total(items,"SUMMER10")
assert p.process_payment(s,items,"SUMMER10")
assert p.transaction_history[0]["charged_amount"] == expected, p.transaction_history[0]["charged_amount"]

issues.title: validate_cart checks each entry separately, not the total per item
issues.explanation: The docstring says stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item_id, and that the same item_id may appear in several entries. The code checks each entry alone. A cart can pass even when its combined quantity exceeds stock. process_payment then charges the full price, but deduct_stock silently skips the entry that no longer fits. The customer pays for goods that are never deducted from stock.
issues.example: Cart [{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}] against a stock of 10 is accepted.
issues.fix: Sum the quantities per item_id first, then run check_stock on each total.
issues.test_code:
pp = PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(), InventoryService())
cart = [{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}]
assert pp.validate_cart(cart) is False, pp.validate_cart(cart)

issues.title: ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting is ignored
issues.explanation: The docstring says a discount code is applied only when ENABLE_DISCOUNTS is on. The code never reads that setting, so discounts are applied even when it is switched off.
issues.example: ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", False); calculate_total([{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":1}], "SUMMER10") returns 26.32 instead of 29.25.
issues.fix: Wrap the discount block in `if ConfigurationRegistry.get("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True):`.
issues.test_code:
ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", False)
pp = PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(), InventoryService())
r = pp.calculate_total([{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":1}], "SUMMER10")
ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True)
assert r == 29.25, r

issues.title: charged_amount records the raw subtotal, not the amount charged
issues.explanation: The docstring says charged_amount is the amount actually charged, as returned by calculate_total. The code stores raw_subtotal, which has no discount and no tax. total_amount is computed and then never used. AuditService.verify_user_totals therefore returns wrong sums.
issues.example: Paying for 1 Mouse (25.0) with no discount records 25.0, but calculate_total returns 29.25.

issues.title: validate_cart checks stock per entry, not per total item quantity
issues.explanation: The docstring says stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item, and the same item_id may appear in several entries. Each entry is checked alone. Two entries of 6 laptops both pass against a stock of 10. The payment then succeeds, and deduct_stock silently skips the second deduction. The customer is charged for 12 units, but only 6 are deducted from stock.
issues.example: [{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}] with stock 10 returns True. process_payment also returns True, and stock ends at 4.

issues.explanation: The docstring says discount codes apply only when ENABLE_DISCOUNTS is on. The code never reads the setting, so discounts apply even when it is off.
issues.example: ConfigurationRegistry.set('ENABLE_DISCOUNTS', False); calculate_total([{'item_id':'item_02','quantity':1}], 'SUMMER10') returns 26.32 instead of 29.25.

issues.example: Buying 2 mice (item_02) with VIP20 gives a charged_amount of 50.0. calculate_total returns 46.8.

issues.test_code:
inv=InventoryService();sm=SessionManager();p=PaymentProcessor(sm,inv)
s=sm.create_session('u')

issues.title: Wall-clock time is used, and `utcnow()` is deprecated
issues.explanation: `datetime.utcnow()` returns a naive datetime that follows the system clock. If the clock is adjusted backwards, `delta` is negative and no refill happens until real time catches up. The code assumes the wall clock never goes backwards, and the docstring doesn't promise that. `utcnow()` is also deprecated since Python 3.12.

issues.title: Bucket entries are never evicted
issues.explanation: Every distinct key adds a permanent entry to `_buckets`. With many one-off keys, such as per-IP limiting, memory grows without bound. Entries that have fully refilled could be dropped.
issues.fix: Periodically remove entries whose tokens would have refilled to capacity, or use a TTL/LRU cache.

issues.title: `consume` has no docstring or thread safety, and its edge-case behaviour is undocumented
issues.explanation: The read-modify-write on `_buckets` is not atomic, so it assumes single-threaded use. Concurrent calls could over-admit requests. Requests for zero or negative tokens always return True without recording anything. Requests for more than the capacity always return False. None of this is documented.
issues.fix: Add a lock around the read-modify-write section and document the edge-case semantics.

issues.title: Wall-clock `utcnow()` is deprecated and not monotonic
issues.explanation: The code assumes the wall clock never goes backwards. If the system time is adjusted backwards, no tokens refill until time catches up. Line 45 also stores the earlier timestamp. `datetime.utcnow()` is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime. The class also has no injectable clock, so it is hard to test.
issues.fix: Use `time.monotonic()`, or accept a clock callable in `__init__`, and store floats instead of datetimes.

issues.title: Bucket entries are never evicted
issues.explanation: Every distinct key adds a permanent entry to `_buckets`. With many one-off keys, such as client IPs, memory grows without bound. This assumes the key space is bounded.
issues.fix: Periodically remove buckets that have fully refilled, or use a TTL or LRU cache.

issues.title: Per-key bucket state is never evicted
issues.explanation: `_buckets` gets one entry for every distinct key and nothing ever removes it. A long-running service that keys on user input such as IP addresses will grow without bound. This assumes the key space is bounded, which the docstring doesn't state. Entries for fully refilled buckets could be dropped safely.
issues.fix: Evict buckets that have fully refilled, or entries idle longer than capacity/refill_rate. Alternatively, cap the number of entries with an LRU.

issues.title: Deprecated naive utcnow() and non-monotonic clock
issues.explanation: `datetime.utcnow()` is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime. Wall-clock time can also jump backwards, for example after an NTP adjustment. `consume` then stores the earlier timestamp, so the next refill is computed from a skewed baseline. The code assumes the clock only moves forward. There is also no locking, so concurrent calls from several threads can race on `_buckets`.
issues.fix: Use `time.monotonic()`, or `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, and guard the read-modify-write in `consume` with a lock if threads are used.
